evidence:
peer-invite.lisp:384-390
(code (fnn-pinv-status-code (fnn-pinv-send control-path :issue signed)))
;; The invitation is recorded before it exists anywhere else.
(when (= code +fnn-exit-ok+)
  (fnn-pinv-write-new out signed)
fnn-pinv-write-new (46-51): with-open-file :if-exists :error, finish-output only (no fsync, no directory fsync).
fix: Check OUT is absent, and create it O_EXCL (empty) before sending :issue. Write and fsync it, and fsync its directory, after the owner accepts. On a write failure after acceptance, report the nonce so the row can be revoked.
notes: 10-02 22:22 OUT reserved O_EXCL before the owner records; fsync+dir fsync; friends_feed asserts
reviewer: peer-invite.lisp:384-390 sends :issue to the owner, which records the invitation durably, before fnn-pinv-write-new (46-51) opens OUT with :if-exists :error. Nothing checks earlier whether OUT exists or is writable (no lstat or probe in fnn-pinv-invite). An existing or unwritable OUT therefore fails after the row is recorded and the signed document is lost. A retry draws a new nonce and records another orphan row. fnn-pinv-write-new only calls finish-output, with no fsync of the file or the directory. The record-first order is intentional per the comment, but a pre-check of OUT is missing. The impact is limited to orphan unconsumed invitation rows.
scenario: OUT already exists (a re-run with the same path) or is unwritable. The owner has durably published the invitation row, then with-open-file signals, and fnn-pinv-execute reports a fault (exit 4). The signed document is lost, a live unconsumed invitation row is left that nobody can present, and the operator's retry draws a new nonce, which adds another orphan row. On a crash after 'invitation ... out=' is printed, OUT can also vanish because it was never fsynced.
title: `peer invite` records the invitation with the owner before checking that it can write OUT
